regional_context.broad_setting: eastern tropical South Atlantic, northern Angola Basin, immediately north of the commonly mapped Congo deep-sea fan extent
regional_context.interpretation: The frozen point at 3.8654 S, 3.8549 E sits just north of the approximate 4 S northern boundary used in published Congo Fan summaries and inside its broad longitude range.
known_regional_morphology: Congo submarine channel-levee and turbidite fan system nearby
regional pockmarks and mass-transport features in parts of the margin/fan
water depths in the deep fan/lobe system commonly around 4.7 to 5.0 km

global_grids.name: GEBCO_2026
global_grids.important_boundary: A GEBCO cell is not automatically a direct sonar sounding. The accompanying Type Identifier grid must be checked to distinguish measured data from interpolation/other source classes.

global_grids.name: GMRT
global_grids.important_boundary: Exact highest-resolution source and direct curated multibeam coverage at the frozen point still need to be resolved from GMRT swath polygons/cruise metadata.

regional_direct_acoustic_surveys.published_scale: more than 25,000 km of 2D high-resolution seismic reported for Congo deep-sea fan survey set
regional_direct_acoustic_surveys.regional_coverage: large portions of Congo fan/canyon-channel system

regional_direct_acoustic_surveys.platform: ROV Victor 6000 and RV Pourquoi Pas?
regional_direct_acoustic_surveys.resolution: about 1-2 m vertical/depth map scale for 60 m-altitude ROV surveys; down to about 0.2 m vertical resolution for low-altitude transects
regional_direct_acoustic_surveys.regional_coverage: selected terminal lobe sites of Congo deep-sea fan, not the entire basin

lidar.reason: Airborne bathymetric lidar is useful in shallow clear water; a several-kilometre-deep abyssal target requires acoustic sounding or other marine geophysical methods.

can_say: Global gridded bathymetry exists for the exact frozen point.
Extensive multibeam, sonar, sub-bottom and seismic surveys exist in the broader Congo/Angola Basin system.
The frozen point is geographically close to the northern edge of a major surveyed deep-sea fan system.
cannot_yet_say: A modern direct multibeam swath passes through the exact frozen point.
A pyramid-like or artificial structure exists there.
Any seabed feature is connected to LOVE, EDEM, Giza, Osiris or an ancient relay.

next_gate.name: EXACT_POINT_SWATH_AND_TID_RESOLUTION_V1
steps: Query GEBCO TID/source class at the exact frozen cell.
Query GMRT point value and highest-resolution source at the exact coordinate.
Intersect GMRT curated multibeam swath polygons and cruise tracks with 0, 1, 5, 10 and 25 km buffers around the frozen point.
Search Ifremer/Geo-Ocean and NCEI cruise catalogs for raw bathymetry/seismic tracks intersecting those buffers.
Only after direct-data provenance is known, inspect morphology for relief, pockmarks, scarps, channels, seamounts or geometric anomalies.

sources: Babonneau et al. / Droz et al. Congo fan multibeam literature
Frontiers 2024 Congo canyon-channel bathymetric survey synthesis
Congolobe project / ROV Victor 6000 high-resolution bathymetry publications
